text: San Roque is a town and municipality in the Colombian department of Antioquia, situated in the Northeastern Antioquia subregion at an elevation of 1,475 m (4,839 ft) above sea level. It was founded by Francisco Martinez de Ospina on 8 February 1880 and officially became a municipality in 1884. The town lies between the Nare River and the Nus River, and its establishment was driven by the presence of gold in the surrounding areas. It is located 121 km north of Medellín. San Roque celebrates most of the traditional festivals observed throughout Colombia. In 1911, the Antioquia Railway was constructed, passing near the town and contributing to the local economy, during which time San Roque functioned as a mining center. The town's historical background is a major draw for modern tourists, and it is commonly referred to as "The Land of Cordiality" due to the friendly nature of its residents. San Roque has a tropical rainforest climate (Af) characterized by heavy rainfall throughout the year. This Department of Antioquia location article is a stub.
